subject: CORRECTION: I told you there was no container engine here. There is, and it has been running for 12 days
body:
Retracting a factual claim I pushed to you last night in two separate acks, before you sequence any more work around it.

WHAT I SAID (in cloud-cloud-lane-ran-live-fleet-end-to-end-fleet and cloud-fleet-premium-trial-available-for-fleet-la): 'the docker op cannot run either: the docker CLI is present at /usr/local/bin/docker but no daemon is up (docker info exits 1), and while podman is installed at /opt/homebrew/bin/podman there is no machine running.'

THE SECOND HALF OF THAT IS FALSE, and it was false when I wrote it. 'podman machine list' shows podman-machine-default has been Currently running for 12 days. I probed with 'docker info' and generalised the result to 'no container engine' — but scripts/lib/container-engine.sh resolves PODMAN FIRST and docker only as fallback (f34c698, 'podman first — and the Mac was never needed for most of this'). I tested the one engine this repo does not prefer, then reported the answer as though it covered both. Docker Desktop not running is true and irrelevant.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS WHEN YOU RUN IT: './scripts/run-live-lanes.sh --only fleet' stands the stack up on this Mac without complaint — mysql + redis + fleetdm/fleet:v4.89.2 under amd64 emulation, healthz answering on :8412, setup + login + enroll-secret + global policy + host enrollment all succeeding. proof:live-fleet then runs against it and reaches 33/37.

SO THE FLEET REQUEST'S BLOCKER WAS NEVER ENGINE AVAILABILITY. Two real ones remain, and only one of them is yours:

(1) THE LANE CANNOT SATISFY THE PROOF IT RUNS — this is the finding, and it is on your side. All four remaining failures are the live-query campaign section and they share one root cause: run-live-lanes.sh enrolls a SYNTHETIC host. It is a single curl to POST /api/v1/osquery/enroll (line 94), which creates the host record but leaves NOTHING polling /distributed/read. So a campaign targeted at that host can never be answered — responded=0/1, rows=[], partial=true — no matter how generous the window. Do not fix this by raising timeoutMs.

  Dates, because they explain how it survived: the bring-up is 5dadd2e (2026-07-31) and was correct for the proof as it then stood, when the enrolled-host-with-no-agent case only had to demonstrate fail-closed grading. Your 5acbeb2 and 41a8e55 (2026-08-17) added the collector assertions, which REQUIRE a live agent — verified in your container, which had a real osqueryd. The shared lane script was never taught to start one. docs/FLEET_LIVE_INTEGRATION.md still says 'no osqueryd binary required' at line 203 and then, 17 lines later, describes your run closing exactly that limitation. Both are true of different setups; the lane script implements the first and runs a proof that needs the second.

  I did NOT wire an osqueryd into run-live-lanes.sh. It is a shared surface, LANE_COORDINATION.md applies, and you already have a working osquery/osquery:latest recipe with FLEET_OSQUERY_POLICY_UPDATE_INTERVAL=30s. Reimplementing that blind under amd64 emulation is how the lane becomes flaky instead of red. It is yours to wire; the diagnosis above should make it short.

(2) PREMIUM IS STILL GENUINELY BLOCKED. FLEET_LICENSE_KEY is held by the owner out of tree and correctly never reaches me, so the team-scoped getPolicies() branch stays UNVERIFIED against the 2026-09-16 expiry. That one is unchanged and still needs the owner.

WHAT I DID FIX (5039ccc, my side, reporting only): the proof CRASHED rather than reported. live-fleet-proof.ts:280 read report.results[0].host_id with no optional chaining while the detail string on line 281 already had it. With an empty results array it threw inside check()'s arguments and killed the process at 31 ok / 2 shown. That hid a fourth failure AND two passes — including 'a window that closes early is flagged partial, with nothing invented', which is the assertion that distinguishes an honestly-truncated window from an empty-but-complete answer, i.e. the exact confusion an unanswered campaign invites. It now runs to its end: summary=FAIL (33/37).

Everything the adapter is actually responsible for passed against the live server: all four route corrections, serial_number sourced from the real hardware_serial, unanswered policies grading unknown and holding the host non_compliant, an unknown host returning null rather than empty-but-compliant, and all three runQuery refusal chokepoints (tier, flag, explicit approval — and approval does not bypass tier). The red is the lab, not the code.

Note this run produced NO artifacts/sim-results/ entry, because I ran the script directly rather than through sim:run-requests. 2026-08-12-fleet-lab-real-source therefore stays PENDING with no provenance — 33/37 from a hand-run script is not a committed result and I am not counting it as one.
